findings.summary: Rollback path for ADR-named one-way decisions is not exercised at TDD layer. The two one-way decisions (synchronous commit-before-ack, declarative unique constraint) have behavioral smoke coverage (e2e 3c7f for RPO=0 survival; integration 92c5 for constraint enforcement under concurrency), but no test validates the deployment rollback path — i.e., that the schema migration introducing the unique constraint can be rolled back non-destructively, or that the replication-mode configuration can be reverted. This gap is appropriately deferred to the IPLAN/DPLAN layer, where the migration and standby-config steps can be tested in a non-prod environment.
findings.recommendation: Record an explicit IPLAN-layer action item for the declarative-constraint migration rollback: (1) verify the constraint drop is non-destructive on a non-prod copy before promoting to prod; (2) verify synchronous_commit can be reverted without dropping committed rows. Reference this TDD in the rollback runbook so the ADR traceability is maintained.

findings.summary: The `mapping_store_degraded` counter is labelled by `degradation_type` in both SPEC §6 and case a3d6, but neither document enumerates the allowed values of that label. If `degradation_type` is derived from raw exception class names, network error strings, or any other unbounded source, the label cardinality is unbounded and will cause metric series explosion in any time-series backend with high-cardinality label costs (Prometheus, Datadog, etc.).
findings.recommendation: Enumerate the allowed `degradation_type` label values in SPEC §6 (e.g., unreachable, dns, tls, timeout) and enforce in the implementation that only those values are emitted. Add a TDD assertion to case a3d6 that the emitted `degradation_type` value is a member of the declared allowlist.
